## Overview

The modular workflow lets you compose individual processing functions to
suit your study design and analytical platform. It is designed primarily
for **untargeted LC-MS metabolomics** data with interspersed pooled QC
samples, run-order drift, left-censored and random missingness, and
co-eluting `"mass@rt"` features.

This vignette walks through the complete sequence from raw intensities to
clustered, normalised features in one place. Each step links to its
dedicated module vignette for deeper parameter guidance and edge-case
examples:

1. **Filter by missingness** — [`filter_by_missingness()`](data-filtering.html)
2. **Detect & remove sample outliers** — [`remove_outliers()`](outlier-removal.html)
3. **Log-transform intensities** — [`log1p()`](log-transformation.html)
4. **Impute missing values (RF + LCMD)** — [`hybrid_imputation()`](hybrid-imputation.html)
5. **Correct drift & batch effects (SERRF)** — [`normalise_SERRF()`](serrf-normalisation.html)
6. **Inspect before/after run-order profiles** — [`plot_omics_distributions()`](plot-omics-distributions.html)
7. **Cluster co-eluting features by retention time** — [`cluster_features_by_retention_time()`](feature-clustering.html)

## Preparing the example data

All modular functions operate directly on a single flat data frame where
rows are samples (study samples plus pooled QC rows) and columns contain
sample metadata alongside numeric feature columns.

We use the built-in untargeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset
(`example_metabolomics`): 216 rows (180 study samples in 90 matched
case-control pairs + 36 pooled `"sQC"` samples across 3 batches and 6
plates) and 30 raw positive-intensity features named in `"mass@rt"`
format:

```{r setup}
library(OmicsProcessing)

data("example_metabolomics")
df <- example_metabolomics

dim(df)
table(df$batch, df$sample_type)
```

## Step 1: Filter by missingness

Remove features and non-QC samples exceeding 50% missingness using
iterative filtering. QC rows (`is_qc = TRUE`) are excluded from
missingness calculations and always retained in the output. See
[Data filtering](data-filtering.html) for filtering order options
(`"iterative"`, `"simultaneous"`, `"col_then_row"`, `"row_then_col"`).

```{r step1-filter}
df_filtered <- filter_by_missingness(
  df,
  row_thresh = 0.5,
  col_thresh = 0.5,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df$sample_type),
  filter_order = "iterative"
)

dim(df_filtered)
```

## Step 2: Detect and remove outlier samples

Detect outlying non-QC samples in PCA space using Local Outlier Factor
(LOF), temporarily imputing missing values with half the column minimum
and restoring original `NA`s afterward. Because `example_metabolomics`
has batch offsets before normalisation, stratifying by `"batch"`
identifies outliers cleanly within each batch (catching all three
injected per-batch outliers). See [Outlier removal](outlier-removal.html)
for PCA + LOF diagnostics and unstratified vs stratified options.

```{r step2-outliers}
outliers <- remove_outliers(
  df_filtered,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df_filtered$sample_type),
  strata = "batch",
  method = "pca-lof-overall",
  impute_method = "half-min-value",
  restore_missing_values = TRUE,
  return_ggplots = FALSE
)

df_clean <- outliers$df_filtered
outliers$excluded_ids
dim(df_clean)
```

## Step 3: Log-transform features

Apply `log1p()` across all `"mass@rt"` feature columns to reduce
right-skewness while handling zeros safely. See
[Log transformation](log-transformation.html) for details.

```{r step3-log}
df_clean <- df_clean %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(tidyselect::contains("@"), log1p))
```

## Step 4: Hybrid imputation (RF + LCMD)

Impute missing values in non-QC samples by fitting Random Forest
(`missForest`) and Left-Censored Missing Data (`imputeLCMD`), selecting
RF for features with OOB error below `oobe_threshold = 0.1` and LCMD
otherwise. QC rows are excluded from model fitting via `is_qc`. See
[Hybrid imputation](hybrid-imputation.html) for QC imputation strategies
and engine control options.

```{r step4-imputation}
set.seed(42)

imp_res <- hybrid_imputation(
  df_clean,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df_clean$sample_type),
  method = "RF-LCMD",
  oobe_threshold = 0.1,
  control_RF = list(verbose = FALSE)
)

df_imputed <- imp_res$hybrid_rf_lcmd
table(method_used = ifelse(imp_res$oob < 0.1, "RF", "LCMD"))
```

## Step 5: Batch and drift normalisation with SERRF

Normalise technical run-order drift and batch/plate shifts using SERRF
trained on pooled QC samples within each batch (`strata_col = "batch"`).
See [SERRF normalisation](serrf-normalisation.html) for tuning guidance.

```{r step5-serrf}
df_normalised <- normalise_SERRF(
  df_imputed,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df_imputed$sample_type),
  strata_col = "batch"
)
```

## Step 6: Visual check before and after normalisation

Inspect a random sample of three features across run order before and
after SERRF normalisation with `plot_omics_distributions()` (note that it
returns the plot invisibly, so assign and print `p`). See
[Normalisation plot comparison](plot-omics-distributions.html) for
progressive plotting layers and interpretation tips.

```{r step6-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6.5}
target_cols <- resolve_target_cols(df_normalised, "@")

set.seed(1)
sample_features <- sample(target_cols, 3)

p <- plot_omics_distributions(
  df = df_imputed,
  df_comp = df_normalised,
  target_cols = sample_features,
  run_order = "run_order",
  is_qc = "is_qc",
  batch = "batch",
  plate = "plate",
  title = "Before normalisation",
  title_comp = "After normalisation"
)
p
```

## Step 7: Cluster co-eluting features by retention time

Group features with similar retention times (`rt_height = 0.07`) and
summarise highly correlated co-eluting features (e.g., adducts or
isotopes) into synthetic PC1 representatives while excluding QC rows
from the output. See [Feature clustering](feature-clustering.html) for
both `"correlations"` and `"scores"` summarisation methods.

```{r step7-clustering}
clusters <- cluster_features_by_retention_time(
  df = df_normalised,
  target_cols = "@",
  is_qc = grepl("^sQC", df_normalised$sample_type),
  rt_height = 0.07,
  method = "correlations",
  cut_height = 0.26,
  corr_thresh = 0.75
)

dim(clusters$clustered_df)
clusters$representatives_map
```

The resulting `clusters$clustered_df` contains study samples with all
metadata columns preserved alongside the final set of normalised,
deduplicated features ready for downstream statistical analysis.
